info.title: Package Guard — supply-chain guard for AI coding agents
info.description: Deterministic pre-install checks for AI coding agents, no LLM. Registry existence (a name npm or PyPI does not have returns likely_hallucination: true, which means only that; private and renamed packages read the same way), known vulnerabilities and malware from OSV.dev, age and weekly-download signals, deprecation, license. Package contents are never fetched or analysed. check-vulns covers all seven OSV ecosystems; the other endpoints resolve names against npm, or PyPI with ecosystem=pypi, so they are npm and PyPI only.

get.summary: Pre-install guard: verdict on whether a package is safe to install
get.description: npm and PyPI only. Returns exists (false means the registry has no such name: likely_hallucination is set, and on npm a 'did you mean' suggestions list comes with it; PyPI names get an empty list). The flag cannot tell an invented name from a typo, a rename, or a package that only exists in a private registry. Also returns OSV vulnerabilities and malware, slopsquat signals (age, weekly downloads, and on npm a name within 2 edits of a search hit), deprecation, license, and a verdict of safe, caution or danger. vulnerabilities.checked=false with count=null means the OSV lookup failed and the package was NOT checked; the verdict is downgraded to caution. count=0 means OSV answered and had nothing.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: npm or pypi. The other OSV ecosystems are accepted by the server but resolve the name against npm, which gives a wrong answer. Use /api/check-vulns for those.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Version to check vulns against (default latest).

get.description: The only endpoint that is correct for all seven ecosystems: it is a straight OSV.dev query and touches no package registry. An empty list means OSV had nothing for that name and version, not that the package is safe. A failed OSV request returns 502, never an empty list.

get.summary: Registry metadata: latest, deprecated, license, repo, downloads, age
get.description: Reads the npm registry, or PyPI with ecosystem=pypi. Weekly downloads come from api.npmjs.org and pypistats.org and are omitted when those are unavailable. 404 with exists=false means the registry has no such name.

npm and PyPI only. Checks the names you send and nothing else: no lockfile is parsed and no transitive dependency is resolved. First 40 names (truncated=true past that). If the batch OSV call fails, every package reports vulns=0. This endpoint does not yet flag an unchecked lookup the way verify-package does.

post.description: Reads the dependencies and devDependencies maps out of package.json text, or name/version lines out of requirements.txt. Manifests only: lockfiles are not parsed and the dependency tree is not resolved. A version range is reduced to the digits inside it, so ^4.17.20 is checked as 4.17.20.

get.summary: Generate lookalike names and flag registered/suspicious ones
get.description: npm and PyPI only. Generates up to 20 ASCII variants (deletions, adjacent transpositions, doubled letters, the swaps l/1, o/0, rn/m, -/_, .-, i-l, s-z, and the name with every hyphen or underscore dropped) and reports which are registered. No Unicode homoglyphs. 'suspicious' means the variant is registered and either under a year old or has no creation date in the registry. That is an age signal, not a judgement about the package.
